title: Modular Pluralism: Pluralistic Alignment via Multi-LLM Collaboration

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model steerability towards specific political party and ideology personas using the OpinionQA dataset, and assessing the coverage of diverse ideological perspectives (left/center/right) in generated responses.

Comparing LLM response probability distributions on the GlobalOpinionQA dataset against country-specific survey data (e.g., US, Japan, Nigeria, etc.) and evaluating the impact of continent-specific cultural community LMs.

Evaluating the model's steerability towards specific demographic attributes (race, sex, religion, education, income, and region) by prompting the LLM with personas and measuring alignment against human survey responses in the OpinionQA dataset.

Measuring the coverage of diverse human values using the Value Kaleidoscope dataset (Overton pluralism) and assessing distributional alignment in low- and high-ambiguity moral scenarios using the MoralChoice dataset.
